hash_map.title: Hash Map
hash_map.description: Key-value lookups for O(1) access. Essential for counting, caching, and quick checks.

two_pointers.title: Two Pointers
two_pointers.description: Two cursors moving through a data structure (usually array/string) to satisfy constraints.

sliding_window.title: Sliding Window
sliding_window.description: A window that slides over data to find a subarray satisfying a condition.

prefix_sum.title: Prefix Sum
prefix_sum.description: Pre-computing cumulative sums to answer range queries in O(1).

stack.title: Stack
stack.description: LIFO (Last-In-First-Out) structure. Good for parsing, nested structures, and backtracking.

linked_list.title: Linked List
linked_list.description: Nodes with pointers. Mastery requires pointer manipulation without losing references.

fast_slow_pointers.title: Fast & Slow Pointers
fast_slow_pointers.description: Cycle detection and finding middle elements in linked lists or arrays.

binary_search.title: Binary Search
binary_search.description: O(log N) search on sorted data or search spaces.

heap.title: Heap / Priority Queue
heap.description: O(1) access to min/max element. O(log N) insert/delete.

two_heaps.title: Two Heaps
two_heaps.description: Using a Min-Heap and Max-Heap together, often to track median.

bfs.title: Breadth-First Search
bfs.description: Level-by-level traversal. Best for shortest paths in unweighted graphs.

dfs.title: Depth-First Search
dfs.description: Deep traversal. Best for exhaustive search, tree properties, and backtracking.

backtracking.title: Backtracking
backtracking.description: DFS with state management (Choose-Explore-Unchoose). Generates all possibilities.

merge_intervals.title: Merge Intervals
merge_intervals.description: Handling overlapping intervals. Usually requires sorting by start time first.

cyclic_sort.title: Cyclic Sort
cyclic_sort.description: Sorting arrays containing numbers in range 1 to N in O(N) time.

topological_sort.title: Topological Sort
topological_sort.description: Linear ordering of vertices in a DAG. Used for dependency resolution.

union_find.title: Union Find (Disjoint Set)
union_find.description: Efficiently tracking connected components and cycles.

dynamic_programming.title: Dynamic Programming
dynamic_programming.description: Breaking problems into overlapping subproblems with optimal substructure.

quests.title: Contains Duplicate

hints.low: Use a hash set to store elements you've seen.
hints.medium: Iterate through the array. If element is in set, return true. Else add it.
hints.high: Time O(N), Space O(N).

quests.title: Two Sum

hints.low: You need to find two numbers that add up to target. For each number, the complement is (target - number). Store numbers you've seen in a hash map.
hints.medium: Use a hash map to store seen numbers. For each number, check if its complement exists.
hints.high: What data structure gives O(1) lookup?

quests.title: Valid Anagram

hints.low: Count character frequencies for both strings.
hints.medium: Use a hash map or fixed-size array (26 chars). Increment for s, decrement for t.
hints.high: If counts match (all zero at end), they are anagrams.

quests.title: Group Anagrams

hints.low: Two strings are anagrams if their sorted versions are equal. Use sorted string as key in a hash map, group by key.
hints.medium: What's a canonical form for anagrams? Use it as a hash key.
hints.high: How do you group items by a computed property?

quests.title: LRU Cache

hints.low: Combine HashMap (O(1) access) + Doubly Linked List (O(1) removal/insertion). Map stores key -> node. List maintains order.
hints.medium: You need O(1) get AND O(1) put with eviction. What two data structures combined give this?
hints.high: Classic design problem. What operations does LRU need to be fast?

quests.title: Valid Palindrome

hints.low: Use two pointers, one at start, one at end.
hints.medium: Move inward, skipping non-alphanumeric chars. Compare characters case-insensitively.
hints.high: If chars mismatch, not a palindrome.

quests.title: 3Sum

hints.low: Sort the array first. Iterate i, then use 2-sum (sorted) on the rest.
hints.medium: Fix nums[i], then find pairs (l, r) that sum to -nums[i].
hints.high: Skip duplicates carefully to avoid repeating triplets.

quests.title: Container With Most Water

hints.low: Area = width * min(height_left, height_right). Start pointers at edges.
hints.medium: Move the pointer with the SMALLER height to try and find a taller line.
hints.high: Greedy approach works because width decreases, so we need higher lines.

quests.title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted

hints.low: Since the array is sorted, use two pointers at start and end. If sum > target, move right pointer left. If sum < target, move left pointer right.
hints.medium: Two pointers converging from both ends. Which pointer do you move based on the sum?
hints.high: The array is sorted. What technique exploits sorted order for pair finding?

quests.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock

hints.low: Track the minimum price seen so far.
hints.medium: Profit = current_price - min_price_so_far.
hints.high: One pass O(N). Update max_profit at each step.

quests.title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement

hints.low: Valid window: length - max_count <= k. Expand right.
hints.medium: Track frequency of chars in window. 'max_count' is freq of most common char in window.
hints.high: If invalid, shrink left. Maximize window size.

quests.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters

hints.low: Use sliding window with a set/map to track characters. Expand right, and when you hit a duplicate, shrink from left until valid.
hints.medium: Sliding window pattern. What condition makes the window invalid? How do you shrink?
hints.high: What pattern handles 'longest subarray/substring with a condition'?

quests.title: Max Consecutive Ones III

hints.low: Sliding window. Expand right. If zeros > k, shrink left until zeros <= k.
hints.medium: Maintain a window with at most K zeros. Max width is the answer.
hints.high: Convert problem: Longest subarray with at most K zeros.

quests.title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum

hints.low: Sliding window. Expand right adding to sum. While sum >= target, update min_len and shrink left.
hints.medium: Variable window. When valid (sum >= target), try to make it smaller.
hints.high: O(N) solution using two pointers.

quests.title: Product of Array Except Self

hints.low: For each position, you need product of all elements to the left AND all elements to the right. Compute prefix products and suffix products separately.
hints.medium: Think prefix and suffix products. Can you compute both in O(N) space, or even O(1) extra space?
hints.high: Similar to prefix sum, but with products. How do you handle the 'except self' constraint?

quests.title: Valid Parentheses

hints.low: Use a stack. Push opening brackets. For closing brackets, pop and check if it matches. Stack should be empty at end.
hints.medium: LIFO structure matches the nesting nature of brackets. What do you push? What do you pop?
hints.high: Classic stack problem. Why is a stack the right data structure?

quests.title: Daily Temperatures

hints.low: Monotonic decreasing stack. Store indices.
hints.medium: When current temp > stack top temp, we found a warmer day for stack top.
hints.high: Pop from stack and calculate difference in indices.

quests.title: Min Stack

hints.low: Store pairs of (value, current_min) on the stack. When pushing, the new min is min(value, current_top_min).
hints.medium: How can you track the minimum at each stack state? Think about what extra info to store.
hints.high: You need O(1) getMin. What additional state helps?

quests.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists

hints.low: Use a dummy head. Compare nodes from both lists, append the smaller one, advance that pointer. Handle remaining nodes.
hints.medium: Create a dummy node to simplify edge cases. How do you decide which node to append next?
hints.high: Classic merge operation. What's the invariant you maintain?

quests.title: Reverse Linked List

hints.low: Use three pointers: prev, curr, next. Save next, point curr to prev, move prev to curr, move curr to saved next.
hints.medium: You need to reverse each pointer. What happens if you lose reference to the next node?
hints.high: Classic pointer manipulation. Can you also do it recursively?

quests.title: Linked List Cycle

hints.low: Floyd's Cycle Detection: Use slow (1 step) and fast (2 steps) pointers. If they meet, there's a cycle.
hints.medium: If fast catches up to slow, what does that tell you about the structure?
hints.high: What pattern detects cycles in linked lists with O(1) space?

quests.title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array

hints.low: Binary search. Compare mid with right neighbor or end.
hints.medium: If nums[mid] > nums[right], min is to the right.
hints.high: Otherwise, min is at mid or left.

quests.title: K Closest Points to Origin

hints.low: Calculate distances. Need K smallest.
hints.medium: Max-Heap of size K. If new point is smaller than heap top, pop and push.
hints.high: Or Min-Heap with all points (O(N log N)). Max-heap is O(N log K).

quests.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array

hints.low: Min-heap of size K. Push all elements, pop if size > K. Root is the Kth largest. Alternative: Quickselect.
hints.medium: Keep a heap of the K largest elements. What type of heap? What's at the root?
hints.high: What's the trade-off between heap and quickselect approaches?

quests.title: Top K Frequent Elements

hints.low: Count frequencies with hash map. Use a min-heap of size K. Push (freq, num), pop if size > K. Heap contains top K.
hints.medium: Count first, then use a heap. Why min-heap of size K instead of max-heap?
hints.high: Classic Top K pattern. What's the time complexity?

quests.title: Sliding Window Median

hints.low: Maintain two heaps: max-heap for lower half, min-heap for upper half.
hints.medium: Balance heaps as window slides. Removing from heap is O(N) or O(log N) with lazy removal.
hints.high: Lazy removal: keep track of invalid elements in a map.

quests.title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal

hints.low: BFS with a queue. For each level, process all nodes currently in queue, add their children. Track level boundaries.
hints.medium: Use a queue. How do you know when one level ends and the next begins?
hints.high: Level-by-level traversal. What data structure naturally gives you this order?

quests.title: Word Ladder

hints.low: Shortest path in unweighted graph -> BFS.
hints.medium: Nodes are words. Edges if words differ by 1 char.
hints.high: Pre-process words with wildcard pattern for O(1) neighbor lookup.

quests.title: Diameter of Binary Tree

hints.low: DFS. For each node, longest path is left_depth + right_depth.
hints.medium: Return max depth from each recursive call.
hints.high: Update global maximum diameter at each node.

quests.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree

hints.low: DFS: return node if it's p or q. Recurse left and right. If both return non-null, current node is LCA. Else return non-null child.
hints.medium: Post-order DFS. What does it mean if you find both p and q in different subtrees?
hints.high: Recursive DFS. What information do you propagate up?

quests.title: Number of Islands

hints.low: Iterate grid. When you find '1', increment count and DFS/BFS to mark all connected '1's as visited (change to '0' or use visited set).
hints.medium: Each island is a connected component. How do you mark visited cells?
hints.high: Classic flood fill / connected components. What triggers a new island count?

quests.title: Path Sum II

hints.low: DFS with current path list and current sum.
hints.medium: At leaf: check if sum == target. Add path to results.
hints.high: Backtrack: pop from path list after visiting children.

quests.title: Validate Binary Search Tree

hints.low: DFS with bounds: each node must be in (min, max) range. Left child: (min, node.val). Right child: (node.val, max).
hints.medium: Pass down valid range for each node. What are the bounds for left vs right children?
hints.high: What constraint must every node satisfy? How do you propagate it?

quests.title: Permutations

hints.low: Backtracking: at each position, try all unused elements. Track used elements with a set or by checking if in current path.
hints.medium: Each position can be any unused element. How do you track what's used?
hints.high: Generate all n! arrangements. What constraint must you maintain?

quests.title: Subsets

hints.low: Backtracking: at each index, choose to include or exclude the element. Base case: reached end, add current subset to result.
hints.medium: Classic Choose-Explore-Unchoose. What are your choices at each step?
hints.high: Generate all 2^n combinations. What's the decision tree?

quests.title: Insert Interval

hints.low: List is sorted. Iterate and add non-overlapping intervals.
hints.medium: Merge overlapping intervals with the new one: min(start), max(end).
hints.high: Add remaining intervals after.

quests.title: Meeting Rooms II

hints.low: Sort by start. Use min-heap of end times. For each meeting: if start >= heap root, pop (room freed). Push new end. Heap size = rooms needed.
hints.medium: Track which rooms become free. A min-heap of end times helps. When can you reuse a room?
hints.high: Interval scheduling. What do you need to track to know when rooms free up?

quests.title: Merge Intervals

hints.low: Sort by start time. Iterate: if current overlaps with last merged, extend end. Else, add new interval.
hints.medium: Sort first. How do you detect overlap? When do you merge vs add new?
hints.high: Classic interval problem. What's the first step?

quests.title: Find the Duplicate Number

hints.low: Treat array values as pointers to indices.
hints.medium: Use Floyd's Cycle Detection (Fast/Slow pointers) on the array indices.
hints.high: Or modify array (negate values) if modification allowed.

quests.title: Course Schedule

hints.low: Build graph and in-degree count. BFS from nodes with in-degree 0. Decrease neighbor in-degrees. If all visited, no cycle.
hints.medium: This is cycle detection in a directed graph. What algorithm detects cycles via ordering?
hints.high: Topological sort. What does a cycle mean for course completion?

quests.title: Number of Provinces

hints.low: Each city is a node. 'isConnected' is adjacency matrix.
hints.medium: Union connected cities. Count distinct parents at the end.
hints.high: Can also use DFS/BFS to count components.

quests.title: Redundant Connection

hints.low: Iterate edges. Use Union-Find.
hints.medium: If two nodes are already in same set (find(u) == find(v)), this edge creates a cycle.
hints.high: Return the first edge that creates a cycle.

quests.title: Network Delay Time

hints.low: Dijkstra's algorithm: min-heap of (time, node). Pop minimum, update neighbors if shorter path found. Answer is max time to reach any node.
hints.medium: Shortest path from source to all nodes. What algorithm with a min-heap?
hints.high: Weighted graph shortest path. When do you update distances?

quests.title: Climbing Stairs

hints.low: DP: ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2). You can reach step n from step n-1 or n-2. Base: ways(0)=1, ways(1)=1.
hints.medium: How many ways can you reach step n? Think about where you could have come from.
hints.high: Classic DP. What's the recurrence? (It's like Fibonacci)

quests.title: Coin Change

hints.low: DP: dp[amount] = min coins to make amount. For each coin, dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[i-coin] + 1). Init dp[0]=0, rest=infinity.
hints.medium: For each amount, try all coins. What's the minimum if you use each coin?
hints.high: Classic unbounded knapsack variant. What's your state and transition?

quests.title: House Robber

hints.low: DP: dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + nums[i]). Either skip house i or rob it (can't rob i-1 then).
hints.medium: At each house: rob it or skip it. If you rob, you can't rob the previous. What's the recurrence?
hints.high: 1D DP with a constraint. What are your two choices at each step?

quests.title: Longest Common Subsequence

hints.low: 2D DP: if chars match, dp[i][j] = 1 + dp[i-1][j-1]. Else, dp[i][j] = max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]).
hints.medium: Compare characters at each position. Match: diagonal + 1. No match: max of left or up.
hints.high: Classic 2D DP. What are your states? What's the recurrence?

quests.title: Maximum Subarray

hints.low: Kadane's Algorithm: At each position, decide whether to extend the previous subarray or start fresh. current_sum = max(nums[i], current_sum + nums[i])
hints.medium: At each element, you have two choices: start a new subarray or extend the existing one. Which is better?
hints.high: This is a classic DP problem. What's the recurrence relation?

quests.title: Final Pattern Scan
quests.instructions: For each pattern, write: trigger, complexity, one example problem.

quests.title: Pattern Review Quiz
quests.instructions: For each of the 14 patterns, explain when to use it and write the template from memory.

quests.title: Pre-Interview Confidence Check
quests.instructions: Rate yourself 1-5 on each topic area. Identify any remaining weak spots.

quests.title: Mock Coding Interview
quests.instructions: Pick a fresh problem from LeetCode Top 100. Time yourself. Speak aloud. Follow DIVE protocol.

achievements.name: Speed Demon
achievements.description: Complete a medium problem in under 15 minutes
